practices_evaluation.justification: The test contains a single object construction but no Arrange-Act-Assert structure or assertions. Although there is only one 'Act' operation, there is no assertion block to validate a single behavior, so it fails the requirement of a clear single Arrange-Act-Assert atomic test.

The test uses only local variables and does not reference or modify any shared static/instance state in the method. No @Before/@After are required for this simple test, and there are no numbered test names or apparent inter-test dependencies.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: Only a single happy-path action (constructing Grafo) is present and there are no tests for error conditions or exception handling. There is no @Test(expected=...) or assertThrows usage.
The test only constructs a Grafo with no input parameters or numeric/string inputs to validate boundaries; boundary-value analysis is not relevant to this simple constructor invocation.
The test is very short and self-contained; there is no duplicated setup across multiple tests in the visible snippet and no helper methods are required for its simplicity.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test is short (<20 lines), linear, and contains no loops or conditionals, satisfying the low complexity requirement.
There are no assertions at all, let alone comprehensive assertions verifying multiple properties of the result. The test does not verify multiple aspects of the created object.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods in the visible code; the test is active and runnable.
The test method includes a Javadoc comment explicitly referencing REQ-001 and a Given-When-Then description, providing traceability to a requirement.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses a timeout on the @Test annotation (@Test(timeout = 4000)), which is an explicit timing constraint; per rules this counts as an explicit performance-related assertion.

The method name 'test0' is generic and does not follow descriptive naming conventions (methodName_scenario_expectedResult). While the Javadoc is descriptive, the name itself is not informative as required.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The file header explicitly states it was automatically generated by EvoSuite and the test method name is generic (test0), both strong indicators of heavy code generation rather than minimal, intention-revealing tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes a Given-When-Then description in the Javadoc, showing evidence of a designed scenario and intention; thus it demonstrates prioritized design intent.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public API (constructor) and does not use reflection or inspect private state; it focuses on observable behavior, which supports maintainability.
There are no assertions at all in the test, so assertions are neither specific nor descriptive; the test fails to use assertions effectively to detect faults.
The test contains a concise Javadoc describing the requirement and Given-When-Then; there is no excessive or commented-out code and comments add value rather than clutter.
The test uses no sources of non-determinism (no Random, time, sleeps, or external dependencies) in the visible method body, so it should be deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only creates a local Grafo instance and does not persist data, modify static state, or leave open resources, so it avoids side effects.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), demonstrating use of test categorization labels for organizing tests.

practices_report.description: Each test case must focus on a single requirement or behavior.
Test cases should not depend on other tests or on execution order.

practices_report.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_report.description: Test cases must check both normal and edge case scenarios.
Tests should validate inputs at the minimum, maximum, and just outside boundaries.
Tests should be self-contained and reusable with helper methods to eliminate duplication.

practices_report.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_report.description: Keep test cases small and focused with low cyclomatic complexity.
Assertions should be comprehensive and verify all relevant properties of the result.
Avoid @Ignore or commented-out tests; keep tests active and runnable.
Each test should be linked to a requirement via annotations or Javadoc.

practices_report.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_report.description: Include performance and security tests when relevant; use timeouts for performance.
Test names should describe the scenario and the expected outcome.

practices_report.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_report.description: Generated test code should be minimal and focused; avoid verbose auto-generated tests.

practices_report.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_report.description: Tests should show evidence of thoughtful design (Given-When-Then, BDD naming).

practices_report.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_report.description: Tests should focus on observable behavior via public APIs and avoid implementation details.
Use clear, specific assertions with descriptive failure messages where appropriate.
Comments should explain why and be minimal; avoid commented-out code.
Avoid random values, time-dependent calls, and external dependencies without mocking.

practices_report.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_report.description: Tests must not modify shared state or leave resources uncleaned.

practices_report.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_report.description: Use @Tag/@Category to organize and classify tests.
